title: 12 — Databricks Hands-On from Zero
html:
12 — Databricks Hands-On from Zero

The one idea: the fastest way to understand Databricks is to build one small, complete pipeline yourself: files in a volume, a Bronze table, a cleaned Silver table, a Gold aggregate, a scheduled job, and a dashboard. This chapter walks through it on the free edition, one lab at a time.

1. What it is

A sequence of eight labs on Databricks Free Edition: serverless-only, one 2X-Small SQL warehouse, up to five concurrent job tasks, one active pipeline per type, and a daily compute quota (per the docs, checked 2026-10-26). Each lab builds on the last. All data is made up.

The SQL and Python below are not run in this note's build environment (there was no Databricks workspace). They use documented syntax. If a command fails, check the linked docs for your workspace's version.

2. Why it matters

Reading about Unity Catalog, Lakeflow and Jobs is not the same as making them work together. After these labs, every other chapter in Data Engineering and Open Lakehouse has a concrete picture behind it.

3. The labs

---
title: The pipeline you build in these labs
---
flowchart LR
    CSV["CSV files<br/>(made-up NAVs)"] --> VOL["Volume<br/>/Volumes/learn/raw/files"]
    VOL --> BR["bronze.nav_raw<br/>(read_files, as received)"]
    BR --> SI["silver.nav<br/>(typed, deduplicated, checked)"]
    SI --> GO["gold.nav_monthly<br/>(aggregate)"]
    GO --> DB["Dashboard"]
    JOB["Lakeflow Job<br/>(file arrival or schedule)"] -. "runs" .-> BR
    JOB -. "runs" .-> SI
    JOB -. "runs" .-> GO

Lab 1: Workspace tour (20 minutes)

  1. Sign up for Databricks Free Edition and open the workspace.
  2. Find the sidebar areas:
    • Workspace: your files and notebooks.
    • Catalog: Unity Catalog objects.
    • Jobs & Pipelines: Lakeflow.
    • SQL Editor and Dashboards.
  3. Open Catalog and note the three-level naming: catalog.schema.object.

Lab 2: Catalog, schema and volume (20 minutes)

In the SQL editor:

CREATE CATALOG IF NOT EXISTS learn;          -- if you lack permission, use the catalog your workspace provides
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS learn.raw;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS learn.bronze;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS learn.silver;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS learn.gold;
CREATE VOLUME IF NOT EXISTS learn.raw.files;

Upload two or three made-up CSV files (isin,nav_date,nav) to the volume through Catalog → learn → raw → files → Upload.

Lab 3: Bronze, as received (30 minutes)

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE learn.bronze.nav_raw AS
SELECT *, _metadata.file_path AS source_file, current_timestamp() AS ingested_at
FROM read_files('/Volumes/learn/raw/files/', format => 'csv', header => true);

SELECT source_file, COUNT(*) FROM learn.bronze.nav_raw GROUP BY source_file;

Bronze keeps every row and records which file it came from. Nothing is cleaned here.

Lab 4: Silver, typed and checked (45 minutes)

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE learn.silver.nav AS
WITH typed AS (
  SELECT isin, CAST(nav_date AS DATE) AS nav_date, CAST(nav AS DECIMAL(18,4)) AS nav, source_file, ingested_at
  FROM learn.bronze.nav_raw)
SELECT * FROM typed
WHERE nav > 0 AND length(isin) = 12
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY isin, nav_date ORDER BY ingested_at DESC) = 1;

-- Rows that failed the checks go to quarantine, never silently away.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE learn.silver.nav_quarantine AS
SELECT * FROM learn.bronze.nav_raw
WHERE TRY_CAST(nav AS DECIMAL(18,4)) IS NULL OR TRY_CAST(nav AS DECIMAL(18,4)) <= 0 OR length(isin) <> 12;

Then look at the table's history: DESCRIBE HISTORY learn.silver.nav;.

Lab 5: Gold and a dashboard (30 minutes)

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE learn.gold.nav_monthly AS
SELECT isin, date_trunc('MONTH', nav_date) AS month,
       MIN(nav) AS min_nav, MAX(nav) AS max_nav, COUNT(*) AS days
FROM learn.silver.nav GROUP BY ALL;

Create a dashboard with one line chart of max_nav by month per ISIN.

Lab 6: The same in Python (45 minutes)

Create a notebook, attach serverless compute, and run:

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
nav = spark.table("learn.silver.nav")
(nav.groupBy("isin")
    .agg(F.max("nav_date").alias("latest"), F.count("*").alias("rows"))
    .orderBy("isin")
    .show())

Then rewrite Lab 4 in PySpark using the PySpark cookbook.

Lab 7: A declarative pipeline (60 minutes)

Create a pipeline (Jobs & Pipelines → Create → ETL pipeline) with this SQL file:

CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE nav_bronze
AS SELECT *, _metadata.file_path AS source_file
FROM STREAM read_files('/Volumes/learn/raw/files/', format => 'csv', header => true);

CREATE OR REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW nav_silver (
  CONSTRAINT positive_nav EXPECT (nav > 0) ON VIOLATION DROP ROW)
AS SELECT isin, CAST(nav_date AS DATE) AS nav_date, CAST(nav AS DECIMAL(18,4)) AS nav FROM nav_bronze;

Run it, open the pipeline graph, and read the expectation metrics. Upload one more file and run again. Only the new file is processed.

Lab 8: Schedule it and keep it in Git (45 minutes)

  1. Create a Job with one pipeline task, and add a file arrival trigger on the volume (or a schedule).
  2. Connect a Git folder to a repository and move your SQL and notebooks into it.
  3. Read Lakeflow section 3.4, and describe the job and pipeline in a databricks.yml bundle.

4. Code

All code is inline in the labs above, and not run in this note's build environment.

5. Common mistakes

  1. Cleaning in Bronze. Keep Bronze as received, so you can always reprocess.
  2. Dropping bad rows silently. Quarantine them with a reason.
  3. Forgetting USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA grants when sharing with a colleague (Unity Catalog).
  4. Leaving work only in the UI. Put it in Git, then in a bundle.
  5. Exhausting the free quota with large range() experiments. Keep data small.

6. Exercise

Complete all eight labs (about 5 hours in total). Then add a second source file format (JSON) to Bronze, and make Silver handle both.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. What does _metadata.file_path give you in Bronze?
  2. Why does QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() ... = 1 deduplicate?
  3. What does ON VIOLATION DROP ROW do, and what does it record?
  4. Why does the streaming table process only new files on the next run?
  5. What does a file arrival trigger replace?

Answers

  1. The source file of each row, which is the start of lineage and of the evidence chain.
  2. It keeps one row per (isin, nav_date), the latest by ingestion time.
  3. It drops rows that fail the rule, and records how many failed in the pipeline's metrics.
  4. It keeps a checkpoint of the files it has already processed.
  5. Polling on a schedule to see whether new files have arrived.

8. Sources

Checked 2026-10-26 through web search.

  • Free Edition limitations: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/getting-started/free-edition-limitations
  • read_files: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/functions/read_files
  • Pipeline expectations: https://docs.databricks.com/ldp/expectations
  • Jobs triggers: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/triggers
